# Five-PR delivery stacks

The current user policy is to accumulate five dependent PRs before integrating the
batch into master. Keep each layer coherent and reviewable. Assemble five layers
before the final combined merge to master.

```text
master ← PR1 ← PR2 ← PR3 ← PR4 ← PR5
```

The bottom PR targets master. Each later PR targets the preceding layer's branch,
so its review shows that layer's change. Use `stack/<batch>-<layer>-<description>`
for batch branches, including the first layer when conserving previews. Preserve the
legacy recreation checkpoint unchanged.

While an earlier layer runs CI, build the next dependent layer when its scope is
clear. Up to five layers may be in flight together. Keep fixes on their owning
branch, propagate them through dependent layers, and validate each resulting head.
Do not open a sixth layer or fold a partial batch into master merely to avoid a wait.

For each finalized PR, create an isolated get-green agent to inspect current-head
Actions and reviews, repair concrete failures and escalate uncertain fundamental
changes to the parent. Pending, missing or failed Actions is not green, but an
intermediate wait does not block assembling the later layers. The merge gate is the
last PR's complete combined head, with a successful named `Rules, build and mock
browser` job and no actionable review findings. Never remove assertions or suites
merely to obtain green checks.

Once five layers exist, assemble all changes on the last PR's branch and target that
PR directly at master. A dependent top branch already contains its ancestors; verify
that ancestry and fold in any missing layer or repair. Validate the final combined
head once instead of waiting for a new CI pass after every intermediate fold. Require
its complete current-head Actions/review gate before the single master merge. Earlier
open layers can target master so their included commits are accounted for by that
combined merge. If master changes during the batch, integrate it and validate the
resulting tree before the final merge. Verify the fetched head and resulting tree;
do not infer completion from a queued operation.

## Vercel deployment budget

Stacking alone does not suppress preview builds. `vercel.json` sets
`git.deploymentEnabled["stack/**"]` to false, using Vercel's supported minimatch branch
rules. Pushes to those batch branches therefore skip automatic Vercel deployments.
Unspecified branches retain their normal behavior, including master. Keeping every
layer under `stack/**` leaves the one master merge as the automatic production
deployment for a batch. A deliberate preview on another branch remains optional.

See [Vercel's Git configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration).
Do not add a broad true rule overlapping `stack/**`: Vercel deploys when any matching
rule enables it. A deliberate intermediate preview skip is expected; continue to
require Actions and reviews. Only the previously observed daily deployment-quota
failure is waived. Investigate other actual deployment failures, and do not retry
deployments or change billing as a response to quota exhaustion.

Validate repository configuration before pushing and inspect provider feedback to
confirm the intended skip. Configuration validity alone does not prove that Vercel
honored the branch rule. No provider account, production-branch or billing setting is
changed by this repository rule.

# Five-PR delivery stacks

The current user policy is to accumulate five dependent PRs before integrating the
batch into master. Keep each layer coherent and reviewable. Assemble five layers
before the final combined merge to master.

```text
master ← PR1 ← PR2 ← PR3 ← PR4 ← PR5
```

The bottom PR targets master. Each later PR targets the preceding layer's branch,
so its review shows that layer's change. Use `stack/<batch>-<layer>-<description>`
for batch branches, including the first layer when conserving previews. Preserve the
legacy recreation checkpoint unchanged.

While an earlier layer runs CI, build the next dependent layer when its scope is
clear. Up to five layers may be in flight together. Keep fixes on their owning
branch, propagate them through dependent layers, and validate each resulting head.
Do not open a sixth layer or fold a partial batch into master merely to avoid a wait.

For each finalized PR, create an isolated get-green agent to inspect current-head
Actions and reviews, repair concrete failures and escalate uncertain fundamental
changes to the parent. Pending, missing or failed Actions is not green, but an
intermediate wait does not block assembling the later layers. The merge gate is the
last PR's complete combined head, with a successful named `Rules, build and mock
browser` job and no actionable review findings. Never remove assertions or suites
merely to obtain green checks.

Once five layers exist, assemble all changes on the last PR's branch and target that
PR directly at master. A dependent top branch already contains its ancestors; verify
that ancestry and fold in any missing layer or repair. Validate the final combined
head once instead of waiting for a new CI pass after every intermediate fold. Require
its complete current-head Actions/review gate before the single master merge. Earlier
open layers can target master so their included commits are accounted for by that
combined merge. If master changes during the batch, integrate it and validate the
resulting tree before the final merge. Verify the fetched head and resulting tree;
do not infer completion from a queued operation.

## Vercel deployment budget

Stacking alone does not suppress preview builds. `vercel.json` sets
`git.deploymentEnabled["stack/**"]` to false, using Vercel's supported minimatch branch
rules. Pushes to those batch branches therefore skip automatic Vercel deployments.
Unspecified branches retain their normal behavior, including master. Keeping every
layer under `stack/**` leaves the one master merge as the automatic production
deployment for a batch. A deliberate preview on another branch remains optional.

See [Vercel's Git configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration).
Do not add a broad true rule overlapping `stack/**`: Vercel deploys when any matching
rule enables it. A deliberate intermediate preview skip is expected; continue to
require Actions and reviews. Only the previously observed daily deployment-quota
failure is waived. Investigate other actual deployment failures, and do not retry
deployments or change billing as a response to quota exhaustion.

Validate repository configuration before pushing and inspect provider feedback to
confirm the intended skip. Configuration validity alone does not prove that Vercel

```markdown
## Summary

<diagram, diff-sketch, or tree>
```

## Sections

Skip all preambles and keep prose brief. Use the user's domain language from `GLOSSARY.md`.

### Summary

Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear.

- Show logic or an algorithm as pseudocode:

```text
on(save)
  if content is unchanged
    return cached result
  write new content
  return fresh result
```

- Show runtime control flow as a call tree:

```text
submitForm
  createSession
    persistPrompt
    launchAgent
  navigateToSession
```

- Show UI structure as a component tree, including state and module boundaries that matter:

```text
<SessionPage> (apps/example/src/routes/session.tsx)
  useSessionEvents()
  <SessionToolbar>
    <RunSkillButton> (packages/ui)
```

- Show file responsibility or a broad refactor as a shallow file tree:

```text
src/
├── commands/       # parses user actions
├── sessions/       # owns session state
└── transport/      # sends API requests
```

- Show component interaction, control flow, or data flow with Mermaid:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI
    participant Daemon
    User->>UI: choose command
    UI->>Daemon: send expanded prompt
    Daemon-->>UI: stream result
```

- Use `diff` when the point is what changes and the surrounding shape already exists. Match the diff shape to the topic.

For a component change:


For a file-layout change:

```diff

+│   └── show-me.ts       # expands the slash command

-└── transport.ts
+└── transport/
+    ├── client.ts

```


```ts
function expandSkill(command: string): string {
```

#### Guidance

Place each visual next to the short text it supports. Keep only the calls, files, props, states, and boundaries needed to answer the user's current question or the options to resolve the current discussion point.

You may use one of these, you may use several, it is unlikely you will use all of them. Use your judgement and don't overwhelm the user.

### Evidence

Concrete evidence that the change works. Show a before and after.

Screenshots are S-tier - when the environment is set up for it and the change is visual.

Execution-based evidence is A-tier. Test results, console output. Show the exact test that now fails and passes, using pseudocode.

### Merge Danger

Describe whether it's a one-way or two-way door. You can walk back through two-way doors, but not one-way doors. A PR that is cheap to roll back is lower risk. Changes that involve destructive actions or hard-to-reverse decisions are one-way doors.

The blast radius is the potential impact or scope of the changes introduced by this PR. Consider all possibilities. Examples are layout shift, breakages for consumers, mobile responsiveness, etc.
# Fidelity ledger

1. The decompiled ActionScript in `../documented-bubble-tank-3/re/bt3/export_scripts_deobf/scripts/`.
2. Verified research documents, especially `research/02-core-gameplay.md` through `05-enemies-waves-difficulty.md`.
3. The Ruffle captures in `research/screenshots/` and `research/08-visual-reference.md`.
4. Earlier exported tables and dossier summaries when they do not conflict with the source.

The imported catalog contains 93 parts, 31 avatar templates, 43 enemies, one boss, two separately recovered ally designs, and 99 wave options. Wave rules, distance conditions, roster batches, mounted geometry, and original encrypted codes are retained.

Retired community queries, sharing/ratings, online accounts, parts-pack purchase/download, advertising/analytics, and external portal medals/stat calls do not run. The menu uses the local library in place of unavailable online tools; obsolete Flash permission tutorials, sponsor redirects, and dead website links are omitted.

Artwork is not downloaded or bundled. Mock mode uses procedural paint, with recovered body/weapon/module timelines and projectile dimensions. Its simplified contours, highlights and animation remain distinct from the supplied original artwork.

- Damage parameters coerce to signed integer before weaken. Forcefield overflow recursively calls Damage, so an artificially combined weaken/forcefield state doubles overflow again; the shipped forcefield blocks acquiring weaken, making this an extension-contract case. `_‑9E` gates player hurt sounds for seven decrements plus the zero-to-minus-one frame; pause/transit suspend that tank clock. Infection's `_‑bN` runs before `_‑J1` clears weaken on its final active frame. Class armor remains UI-only, as in the source.

- `PauseMenu._-Bz` groups categories2/3/5 by type, sorts IDs, and switches each category to short names only when it has more than two distinct types. Single full names have no count prefix; plural labels use the imported `strPluralName`. `_‑cG` displays class speed and armor rather than current life or creator budgets, and reparents the existing avatar. The shared `TankView` paints the same mounted rotations, hidden/removed parts, status, and protection state for gameplay and the frozen Info portrait. `_‑HP` and `_‑U0` supply the panel motion; pause-orb choreography remains an approximation.
- `_‑EG`/symbol2276 has no statistics or dynamic TextFields. Its 39 preparation frames perform19 blur passes; frame40 starts2275 atframe2, fading through24 and stopping at25. Continue restores play; Main Menu leaves the run. Numerical placements and alpha values come from `tools/import-win-geometry.ts`; the original pack-manager control and promotional copy are omitted through that importer.

- `_-14/_-6.as` freezes Apocalypse at the visual bubble wall while its fuse runs; it does not immediately kill the field. `_-MC` (2173) ends after 120 frames; `_-0D.ShrinkBubblefield` subtracts 1/204 scale each frame. The implementation marks the field destroyed and escapes at the end. Reward/transition choreography still needs a runtime comparison.
- `_-14/_-JX.as` retains its orbital projectile kind while pursuing a target, steers back by signed angle/20 outside the ring, and turns 5 degrees within it. `_-9U` and `_-Vc` pass radians + 90 to the degree-based spawn API; that quirk is retained. Opposing shots survive shooting down these seekers.
- `_-14/_-Kk.as` gives rockets a randomized 0.10–0.20 sine frequency and 0.1–0.8 radian amplitude with counter starting at 45. `_-14/_-dO.as` jitters movement around its original heading rather than accumulating rotation.
- Projectile symbol/scale mappings are imported from the actual `SpawnNewBullet` call sites into `projectile-art.json`. Sapper/mine state frames are selected explicitly rather than playing through unrelated timeline states.
- `_-14/HealerBeam.as` and its pcode advance healing after eleven pixel-contact frames and preserve the counter across interruptions. The unusual `sqrt(dx * dx + dy + dy)` integer prefilter is retained. `_-ct/EBehaviorHealer.as` owns a patient independently of offensive targeting, updates its beam every three frames, and stops it beyond 400 pixels.
- `_-14/_-CO.as` damages after two contact frames, retaining partial contact across interruptions. Every target uses the same six-pixel sampling grid starting at the truncated minimum center-distance minus radius; the signed sine broad-phase quirk is retained. Beam children use the source's line width, mask width plus four, and endpoint position.
- `_-ct/_-DO.as`, `EnemyTurret.as`, and `EnemyTurretBuilder.as` build four stages at the weapon registration point, use straight builders, retain completed turrets while starting another, and preserve opposing shots that intercept builders. A completed turret shields its owner; its stopped inner view turns toward the owner.
- SWF `StateNewStyles` appends a new indexed style table and starts a new paint layer. Shape 683 demonstrated the previous error: merging old edges into new colors canceled the center under even-odd filling. The parser now keeps style offsets/layer order, reverses fill-left edges, joins directed boundaries, and omits internal edges shared by the same fill.
- `_-Zx.Run` pauses jam, ink, weaken, infection, and enemy movement's sticky timer while stunned, while attached effect clips and forcefield recharge continue. Infection's counter starts when infected and damages every twelve active frames; forcefield replenishment counts twenty frames with damage debt. Neither counter is tied to tank age.
- `_-Zx.EffectMeCrazy` replaces earlier marks, places one per part below five parts, and otherwise picks five parts with replacement. Sticky/jam/weaken hold a randomized variant while nested clips keep playing; stun plays from a randomized starting frame. `_-U4` supplies the infection overlay, random rotation, and color matrix. `_-ar` applies ink only to the avatar without refreshing an existing timer; a forcefield suppresses its visual effect while retaining its timer. The ink clip has its own authored 100-frame lifetime.
- `BTAGameWorld.AttachNewBubblefield` skips only stored `"destroyed"` fields, not ordinary cleared fields. Its transit layout uses the exterior mask's authored 1391.9px width, not the visible bubble's 847.5px diameter; geometry is imported by `tools/import-swf-geometry.ts`.
- `AGunShield` uses the 25-frame `_-YE` effect as its lifetime, with `_-BF` display art and the directional `_-Ne` impact. The turret shield uses `_-bM` and `_-KJ`. `APassiveForcefield` clips its splash to a cloned full design; `forcefieldanimation_551` stops at frame 1, returns there at 25, loops broken frames 26–34, and rearms from 36.
- Morph edge records contain empty style arrays; spreading those records after the tag's styles erased every morph's fills/strokes. The tag parser now preserves those styles, end gradient offsets/focal values, and signed FIXED8 fields. Interpolation pairs edges across differing run boundaries and converts straight/curved pairs to quadratics. Gradient matrix coefficients retain eight decimal places.
- `TankCreatorScreen._-L3` toggles individual selected parts without requiring Shift; `SelectObject` also selects and fades a linked twin. `_‑bp` adds parts whose center/cardinal radius samples intersect the marquee, retaining its duplicated positive half-Y sample. `StartDrag` records which side of the initial pointer each selected part occupies and `_‑5M` mirrors the movement on the other side. `_‑CI` sets every selected scale absolutely; `_‑aJ` sets absolute rotations with sign determined by Y. `DeleteObject` removes only that object and breaks its surviving twin's link; `_‑6z` unlinks partially selected pairs after editing. `SymmetricModeMouseUp` clears selection. The recreation keeps this transient selection state outside serialized designs.
- `StartDrag` samples its grab offset on the first move, while preserving the pointer-down side for every selected part. `_-5M` examines pre-move positions, considers the nearest selected part within 0.5 pixels (inside a redundant 3-pixel test), and retains the positive entry delta shown in both ActionScript and AVM2 bytecode. Exact-axis merging removes the faded member of a selected pair, even when it is the pointer-side reference. `RespawnTwinObject` inserts a new reciprocal twin immediately after its owner, copies scale/type/radius, mirrors Y/rotation, fades it, and gives it the opposite drag side. The controller normalizes only browser coordinate roundoff within 0.00001 pixels of zero.
- Live original menu clicks corrected the visual-reference notes: the left plus is Parts Packs, and the right bubble cluster is Enemy Tank Creator. `_‑Sm.mmBtnUp` confirms the handlers; sprite 556 places symbol 496 as `partsPacks_btn` at (145.85,228.7), and symbol 500 as `enemyCreator_btn` at (365.85,228.7). The recreation now places the creator on the right and the deliberate local-library replacement on the left, with matching mock icon shapes.
- `TankCreatorScreen._-3N` initially assigns life/reward/speed1/1/1, but its later enemy constructor call `_‑13:4642–4653` replaces these with20/20/2 and enables suggested settings. The recreation now uses the later20/20/2 defaults, retained suggestion flag, phase-specific save update and authored enemy panel described below; complete constructor/frame ordering comparison remains open. `_‑Jo` changes the selected palette item and preview; `StartLibraryDrag` begins placement from the preview. `_‑8a` snaps new objects at |Y| ≤ 3 even in asymmetric mode and fades a mirrored draft to 25%. `_‑ZW` commits valid members individually, restores their opacity, and does not call `SelectObject`. The selected palette item and any earlier placed-part selection remain available after the drop. Its stored radius is the newly constructed clip's width/2, so raster padding must be excluded.

- `TankCreatorScreen.UpdateAffordableArray` checks one object against complexity, remaining Gun Points, and inclusive class limits independently of symmetry and locks. `_‑ay` sorts by lock state, numeric Gun Point cost, then object ID; `_‑1X` chooses the first affordable unlocked row. `UpdateLibraryButtonsForAffordability` only changes opacity to 0.4, so unaffordable unlocked rows remain selectable and placement is allowed; save validation enforces the final build. Body rows omit cost indicators and free weapons display 0. A native original capture selected the dimmed Class 2 Seekers from a Class 1 design and updated its preview (`/tmp/bt3-original-dim-selection.png`). Mock/SWF browser regressions cover palette ordering, dimmed selection, empty default preview, budget/complexity overflow, and undo.

- Creator `_‑Jo` constructs a new live preview clip; `_‑Zl` constructs separate live drag clips and `_‑ZW` retains them after placement. `UpdateClass` builds a fresh body-only clip through `TankData._‑Tr(4)` for its pixel snapshot. The editor now reuses the native display-list renderer for preview, draft, and placed artwork, keeps per-part ages through edits/drops, and uses matching animated alpha tests. Browser checks require at least three different pixel poses in both a Medium Bubble preview and placed parts while retaining their exported geometry. Two original Ruffle captures showed 985 changed preview pixels and 232 changed placed-part pixels in their respective crops. This confirms animation exists; it does not prove synchronized frame identity or complete MovieClip script semantics.

- Remaining animation-script evidence: `BubbleMedium` and `_‑7E` choose `round(random * 10)` when frame 1 runs; `_‑MQ` branches between its two halves according to Y and loops at 50/100; `_‑Rk` starts at a random frame through 100 and returns to frame 2 at 121. These frame actions now run in the retained clip player used by the creator and live tank artwork. Their boundaries have source-backed unit tests; synchronized original-runtime comparison is still required before claiming complete animation parity.

- `tools/import-timeline-scripts.ts` recovers 230 complete frame-action tables and checks the original SWF's part subtree plus the three mine roots: all 25 scripted part clips and the mine roots are covered. It rejects an unrecovered reachable script rather than partially importing its class. Eighteen other classes contain unsupported callbacks, including application/retired-service code and several projectile effects. The runtime executes typed stop/jump/random/Y-branch data, never ActionScript or arbitrary expressions.
- `ClipTimeline` and `SwfClip` retain per-instance cursors and child lifetimes. Children continue under stopped parents, missed render frames still advance construction/removal in order, and a self-targeting jump does not recurse. `AssetPack` gives each live tank part a retained pose shared by drawing and pixel contact, with a stable private random stream. Creator drops retain their clip instances; adding a cluster restarts existing clusters as `_‑2I` specifies. Class snapshots still stop fresh body clips at frame 2 as `TankData._‑Tr(4)` does.
- The playback fixture compares nine part cases at four ages, including both Wiggle Cluster halves, all other complex bodies, and the stopped Massive Cannon effect. It recorded 3,697 solid-interior pixel samples with zero misses and zero spurious hits against WebGL output; partial-alpha pixels and antialiasing boundaries are excluded. The source loop boundaries and retained-tree construction have ten dedicated unit tests. These checks prove internal pose/contact agreement and recovered transitions, not pixel identity or timing identity with Adobe Flash.

- `AvatarInterface.mapUp` cycles frames 1→2→3→1 without pausing: compact 122.45×94, large 401.45×274, then hidden. `tools/import-swf-geometry.ts` now imports the map's authored centers/scales from sprites 1534/1520. The recreation uses the native map/button/dot artwork, recenters when a destination attaches, and keeps map scale independent of camera zoom. Native captures in the sibling research repository (`30-minimap-large.png`, `31-minimap-hidden.png`) confirm the original cycle. The edit-button anchor follows the source's 124/304/54 Y positions; its exact variants and tween remain part of the HUD work.
- `_‑0D.TestForCompletion` calls `AvatarInterface._‑Ep` (dot frame 3, hollow); `Destroy` calls `_‑39` (frame 2, crossed). Earlier research notes incorrectly called these visited/current states and have been corrected. The source's fixed white point marks the current map center. The reconstruction retains the user's requested deduplication of completed crossings, whereas the original can add repeated connector clips on revisits.
- The minimap fixture renders an uncleared field, a cleared field, a destroyed field, a long path, and adjacent fields without a traversed path. Alpha samples were 255 for a traveled line, 13 for an untraveled gap, 86 for an uncleared fill, 13 for a cleared center, and 247 for a destroyed cross. Pixels beyond the viewport and in hidden mode were zero. A map-specific alpha normalization makes the authored half-alpha vector mask clip by geometry. These checks cover map visibility, symbols, and clipping; they do not establish whole-HUD pixel parity.

- `core/hud.ts` replaces CSS health/fire transitions with `AvatarInterface.InterfaceMotion`: 75-frame idle counters and `0.8 * current + 0.2 * target`. Life starts 100 pixels below its authored position and detects changes after motion; its rest Y includes the source's +0.2 offset. Fire starts 100 pixels above and retreats an additional full panel height. Primary input reveals the panel every held frame, including cooldown/jam; automatic passive shots do not. Secondary input reveals it on an actual shared trigger. Animation advances during crossings and freezes while paused or while Apocalypse suspends player control (source worldstate3).
- `render/hud-view.ts` paints sprites 1438/1506 and their native fill clips, overwriting authored fill scaleX exactly as `_‑MO` does. Primary grouping retains the first mount/counter and its order. Labels come from `_‑HJ.strShortName`; one Basic Cannon is `BC`, repeated cannons are `BC's`. The native firing capture confirms the ActionScript negative-length `substr(0,-2)` suffix removal. No shipped part sets `intMaxCharge`, so unused charge fills stay hidden; Massive Cannon retains its separate secondary charge effect. Dynamic device text uses Arial 10 with the authored spacing/alignment; precise emulator/Flash font metrics remain a comparison gap.
- The HUD fixture covers nine unique rows, repeated primaries, secondary-only and empty-weapon layouts, and partial life/cooldowns. Filled/empty alpha samples were 193/51 for primary/secondary bars and 158/40 for life, verifying the original child/root alpha combination and scale overwrite. Six rule tests cover source easing/order, idle timing, first-mount grouping, held-input behavior, and paused/transit clocks. These prove recovered contracts and artwork placement, not whole-HUD pixel identity.
- The original reference viewer now uses Ruffle 0.7.1 `wgpu-webgl`. Passive REA console capture `ev_cbe3ad7b95a2055c8235996317effafaa2cedfa075b967f758f3022b40198217` exposed repeated `Render backend does not support BitmapData.draw` failures with legacy `webgl`; menus could work while gameplay enterFrame failed. After the backend change, `ev_d1a8953c988b3b60c7e1d6cea06190f8f5e95ac93e696511f11475397ebbb7a0` confirmed the renderer and disappearance of those failures, and native firing capture `ev_9c86274ca7620559022d320dea8d9de526400585e13bc5fe3010f75304245de4` showed the `BC` HUD and live shots. Preserved sibling captures `32-hud-primary-fire.png` and `33-hud-life-spawn.png` show firing and the initial `Basic Tank` / `49 Bubbles left` health widget. The optional smoke test focuses the movie before clicking the native Continue glyph; one first click can otherwise leave the preloader unchanged in the emulator. Retired networking remains blocked. Earlier boot/menu/map checks should not be read as proof that the old reference setup supported full gameplay.

- `BTAGameWorld.AttachNewBubblefield` selects the caption before incrementing `_‑41`. Counter 0 selects `ag`, 1→`tut_2`, 2→`tut_3`, 3→`tut_4`, and later values select `ag`. Only a new destination increments the counter. Home initially gets `tut_1`, but returning home immediately after the first new field replaces it with `tut_2`. Source/pcode ordering and live captures confirm this unusual behavior. Captures `34-first-new-field-ag.png`, `35-home-revisit-tut2.png`, `36-damage-collection-tut3.png`, and `37-pause-options-tut4.png` are preserved in the sibling research repository; REA screenshot evidence is `ev_dffd201c49a2380d3d3963c41792f4613ffc09dd4697c51ba687a6cbd89ecd70`.
- `bfStartDisplay` (1667) holds stopped frames 2–6 with the original static DefineText2/logo children. They remain at field-local (0,0), keep their own scale when the bubble radius changes, and sit below enemies. There is no age-based blink, timeout, or task-based tutorial advancement. The original separate W/mouse artwork, 25px embedded font, 102/255 text alpha and grey tint on lessons 2/3 are retained. The pause lesson keeps its original hardcoded P even after key remapping. Screen-reader text spells out movement and left-mouse input; mock mode uses readable fallback words.
- `AvatarInterface.TriggerEditButton`, `_‑WF`, `_‑H5`, `SetMovement`, `_‑BV` and `_‑Kz` establish the edit control: compact width122 atY124, large width401.45 atY304, hidden-map E width24 atY54. It starts at `-(width+10)` and approachesX24 at `40 or 65 * remainingDistance / initialDistance` per frame, then snaps below0.2px. The source still applies its previous movement after snapping, leaving a small overshoot; the model retains it. `_‑BV` changes a settled tab's frame/position without changing the previous trigger speed. The tab is triggered on completion or attaching an empty field and retracts when a populated destination attaches while it is settled.
- The field-overlay fixture renders all five native caption states with nonzero ink, verifies that doubling field radius preserves the caption pixels and that moving the camera80px shifts them by−80px, and checks all three edit widths. Edit hover changes sampled background alpha51→102. The renderer applies alpha2 to individual leaves because Pixi clamps container alpha while [Ruffle carries the original value as a color-transform multiplier](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/master/core/src/display_object.rs). This adapter follows recovered semantics; whole-image hover comparison with Adobe Flash remains unproven.
- The edit control opens UpgradeMenu's authored frame4 confirmation before the existing same-level selection panel. Choosing a replacement or saving an edit calls the equivalent of `PlaceAvatar(0)`: it replaces the current history slot and restarts health at `floor(maxLife/75)+1`. It no longer preserves the previous health value. NO leaves the run intact, and canceling the current-tank creator resumes it. Native foreground labels, dashed rules and YES/NO states are supplied by the SWF; the complete blur/fade choreography still belongs to remaining screen-transition work.

### Field completion and secondary help

- `_‑0D.TestForCompletion` (1543–1574) suppresses only the initial `blnFirstBubblefield` wrapper and its own `_‑FR` latch. `AttachNewBubblefield` reconstructs both flags; cached empty enemy lists do not preserve completion. `core/field-visit.ts` models that live wrapper separately from persistent `Field.cleared`. Returning to an empty field completes it again, including returning home. `BTAGameWorld.Run` runs both wrappers during state2, so this check happens on the first transit frame rather than arrival. Pausing freezes it. Destroyed fields do not complete. Completed counts and unique minimap paths remain independent.
- Cached fields also lose `blnBossBubblefield`, as in the source. `CompletedABubblefield` checks the **current** wrapper's boss flag even if the next wrapper called it; that source edge case is retained, including `PreWinScreenSetup` declining the win screen during transit while medals still award. Masochist compares the maximum absolute coordinate against the unique-field counter. Exact boss/win transition behavior still needs comparison.

---
name: babysit-pr
description: Monitor a pull request through review and CI. Use when the user asks to monitor, watch, or babysit a PR.
---

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.
---
name: file-pr
description: File a concise pull request. Use when the user asks to file, open, or create a PR.
---

# File PR

Before filing, check whether a PR for this branch already exists. Review the
diff locally against the base branch (usually `origin/main`) to make sure its
contents match the goal.

PR titles usually become commit messages, so follow the repository's title
conventions. Look at recently merged PRs and Git history for examples. Prefer a
concise, human-readable title that explains why the change matters:

BAD

> ❌ perf(server): negotiate permessage-deflate on the websocket

GOOD

> ✅ perf(server): cut websocket frame size by 70%+ with gzipping

Open the description with a simple explanation of the problem based on the
user's original prompt, then briefly explain the solution. Do not lead with an
implementation inventory:

BAD

> ❌ Removed implicit workspace carry-over from every "new thread" entry point (cmd+n / cmd+shift+o, sidebar v1/v2 buttons, command palette). New threads inherit only the project from context; branch, worktree, and env mode always come from the configured defaults. Deleted buildContextualThreadOptions, startNewThreadInProjectFromContext, and the v1 sidebar's seed-context machinery.

GOOD

    for (const [depth, child] of this.children)
